#### Leveling

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Xp Curve (`xpCurve`) | [VtXpCurveDefinition](leveling.md#vtxpcurvedefinition) | None |  | XP curve this unit progresses on. Non-null = VtUnit.SeedFromDefinition auto-attaches a VtUnitLevel component that tracks the unit's level + current XP and fires OnLeveledUp on threshold crossings. The component seeds its starting level from the existing 'startingLevel' field above (under Progression). Null = unit doesn't level (most mobs). |
| Xp Award (`xpAward`) | `int` | 0 | ≥ 0 | XP credited to the killer on this unit's death. > 0 = VtUnit.SeedFromDefinition auto-attaches a VtXpAwarder that subscribes to OnDied and credits the killer's VtUnitLevel. 0 = no awarder attached (most non-combat NPCs). |

#### Immunities

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cc Immunities (`ccImmunities`) | [VtCcCategory](#vtcccategory)[] | Empty |  | Crowd-control categories this unit is innately immune to. Apply-time gate refuses any VtBuffDefinition whose ccCategory matches an entry — the buff silently fails to apply and an Immune combat-text event fires. Use for boss design (Stun + Taunt immunity), boss adds (Fear immunity), racial passives (Undead → Fear/Charm/Sleep immunity). |
| Damage Immunities (`damageImmunities`) | [VtDamageType](#vtdamagetype)[] | Empty |  | Damage types this unit is innately immune to. Damage of an immune type is dropped before any pipeline math (no resist roll, no armor) and an Immune combat-text event fires. Use for elemental boss design (Fire Lord immune to Fire, Frost Wyrm immune to Cold, Lich immune to Shadow). |

#### Innate modifiers / traits

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Innate Modifiers (`innateModifiers`) | [VtItemModifier](#vtitemmodifier)[] | Empty |  | The unit's racial / class baseline for scalar stats — e.g. a Dwarf starts with +2 Armor and +25% Fire Resistance, a Giant starts with +100 MaxHp. Each entry is a (VtStatDefinition, value, isPercentage) triple, same shape as items and buffs use.  Pushed into VtUnitModifiers under the source key "innate" at spawn. Items, buffs, and level-up gains use separate source keys and STACK ON TOP — equipping a +3 Armor ring leaves the Dwarf's innate +2 intact. Unequipping only removes the item's source, the baseline is untouched.  Leave empty for generic units with no racial quirks. |
| Innate Traits (`innateTraits`) | [VtTraitOverride](#vttraitoverride)[] | Empty |  | The unit's racial / class baseline for CATEGORICAL traits (not numeric stats) — e.g. a Ghost has VtMovementType = Flying, a Golem has VtArmorType = Heavy, an Undead has CanMove = true but Sleep-immune. Each entry is a (VtTraitKey, value, priority) triple.  Written at priority 0 so items and buffs (priority ≥1) naturally override — equip a Levitate Amulet and the Golem's VtMovementType flips to Flying for as long as it's worn, then reverts.  Leave empty to accept the default trait values (VtMovementType.Ground, CanMove=true, etc.). |

#### On-Kill / Spawn

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Xp Reward (`xpReward`) | `int` | 0 | ≥ 0 | XP awarded to the killer when this unit dies. |
| Respawn Time (`respawnTime`) | `float` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Seconds before this unit respawns (when used with a respawning spawner). 0 = no respawn. |
| Model Prefab (`modelPrefab`) | `GameObject` | None |  | OPTIONAL. Only used by data-driven spawners (e.g. WaveSpawner) that pick a VtUnitDefinition from a table and need to instantiate a GameObject from scratch. Leave EMPTY when the unit is authored as a scene-placed prefab with its VtUnit component and 'definition' slot already wired — in that workflow the prefab itself carries the visuals, this field is redundant. Typical use: one SkeletonWarrior.asset points at SkeletonWarrior_Model.prefab; a wave spawner looks up the SO, Instantiates modelPrefab, then attaches VtUnit components and sets the definition. Null with a data-driven spawner → spawner falls back to a debug primitive capsule. |

## VtUnitStats

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → Units → VtUnitStats**. Adds [VtUnitModifiers](#vtunitmodifiers) automatically.

Resource pools (HP / MP / Stamina / Rage / Focus / ...) for a unit. Owns the `TakeDamage` pipeline (evade → element resistance → damage matrix → armor → absorb → round → apply) and the pre/post damage hooks.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `IReadOnlyList<VtResourcePool> Pools { get; }` | All resource pools on this unit, in definition order. Do not mutate the list; pool currents mutate via `VtResourcePool.Spend` / `VtResourcePool.Restore`. |
| `float TimeSinceCombat { get; }` | Simulation seconds since the last incoming or outgoing damage. A unit is considered "in combat" for `VtCombatConstants.OutOfCombatThreshold` seconds after any hit. Advances with `Tick`, not wall-clock time. |
| `bool InCombat { get; }` | Whether the unit is currently treated as in combat — drives `VtRegenMode.CombatOnly` / `VtRegenMode.OutOfCombatOnly` pools. Threshold is global (`VtCombatConstants.OutOfCombatThreshold`). |
| `int HP { get; }` | Current health, or 0 without an HP pool. |
| `int MaxHP { get; }` | Maximum health after modifiers, or 0 without an HP pool. |
| `bool IsDead { get; }` | True once the HP pool has hit 0. Units without an HP pool are never dead. While dead, every HP-restoring path no-ops — see `Revive`. |
| `int MP { get; }` | Current mana, or 0 without an MP pool. |
| `int MaxMP { get; }` | Maximum mana after modifiers, or 0 without an MP pool. |
| `int Stamina { get; }` | Current stamina, or 0 without a Stamina pool. |
| `int MaxStamina { get; }` | Maximum stamina after modifiers, or 0 without a Stamina pool. |
| `VtRegenScheduler RegenScheduler { get; }` | The regeneration scheduler behind this component, for advanced use. |
| `event Action<VtDamageInfo> OnPreTakeDamage` | Pre-hook, authority-only. Subscribers may mutate the `VtDamageInfo` (convert element, add to absorbed, set cancelled=true). |
| `event Action<VtDamageInfo> OnPostTakeDamage` | Post-hook, notification. Fires on both authority and replicas after the hit resolves; `VtDamageInfo.appliedDamage` reflects the final value. |
| `event Action<VtDamageInfo> OnPreDealDamage` | Fired on the *attacker* before the target pipeline resolves. VtAuthority-only. |
| `event Action<VtDamageInfo> OnPostDealDamage` | Fired on the *attacker* after the target pipeline resolves. Drives lifesteal, on-hit procs. Notification (fires on authority; replicas get it from their mirror of the attacker if relevant). |
| `event Action<VtUnitId> OnDied` | Fired when HP reaches 0. Notification event. |
| `static event Action<VtUnit, VtUnitId> OnAnyUnitDied` | Static fan-out fired alongside the instance `OnDied` event. Args: (killedUnit, killerId). One subscription covers every unit in the world — used by `VtUnitQuestLog` to advance kill objectives without subscribing to each spawned unit individually. |
| `event Action<int> OnRevived` | Fired after `Revive` brings a dead unit back above 0 HP. Args: the HP the unit was revived with. Notification — respawn VFX, re-enabling AI, clearing "corpse" UI state. Does **not** fire for the `Initialize` re-seed path (that's a fresh spawn, not a revive). |
| `event Action<VtDamageInfo> OnEvaded` | Fired when an incoming hit was dodged (before HP is touched). Notification; drives "Miss!" floating text. |
| `event Action<int, bool, bool, VtUnitId> OnHealed` | Fired after a heal lands on this unit. Args: amount actually restored (post-crit, post-clamp), whether it was a crit heal, whether it came from a HoT tick (vs a direct heal), the applier id. Notification only — drives floating-text / healing log. **Does not** fire for regen; regen is continuous and unimportant to surface as text. |
| `void MarkInCombat()` | Restart the combat timer. The damage pipeline calls this on both defender and attacker when a hit lands; consumers with their own "enter combat" triggers (a taunt shout, an aggro pull) may call it too. |
| `void Initialize(VtUnitDefinition def)` | Seed pools from a `VtUnitDefinition`. Rebuilds every pool at its `startingCurrent`, so a dead unit re-seeded this way comes back alive without firing `OnRevived` — this is the respawn path (fresh spawn semantics), not the in-place resurrection path (`Revive`). Safe to call before any child components bind to events — pools fire their `VtResourcePool.OnChanged` on the first mutation. |
| `VtResourcePool GetPool(VtResourceKind kind)` | Return the pool for `kind`, or null if the unit doesn't have one. Callers that rely on a specific pool should null-check (a basic mob with only HP returns null for MP). |
| `bool HasPool(VtResourceKind kind)` | True if the unit has a pool of this kind. |
| `int TakeDamage(VtDamageInfo info)` | Apply a damage hit through the full pipeline. Returns the final damage dealt (0 on evade / cancel). VtAuthority-only; replicas mirror HP through pool replication and raise the hit events through `ApplyHitFromNet`. |
| `int TakeDamage(int amount, VtDamageType type = VtDamageType.Physical)` | Deal plain environmental damage, such as a trap or a fall, with no attacker. Builds a minimal `VtDamageInfo` of the given `type` and runs it through the full pipeline. |
| `void Heal(int amount)` | Restore HP by `amount` with no crit / applier context. VtAuthority-only. Used by lifesteal and any host code that heals without a meaningful caster. No-op while `IsDead`. |
| `int Heal(int amount, VtUnitId applier, bool canCrit)` | Restore HP with optional crit support. When `canCrit` is true, rolls the applier's `stat.crit_chance`; on success, multiplies by `VtCombatConstants.DefaultCritMultiplier` + `stat.crit_multiplier`. Returns the actual amount healed (after crit scaling). Used by `VtHealEffect` and HoT ticks. VtAuthority-only. Returns 0 while `IsDead`. |
| `int TakeTickHeal(int amount, VtUnitId applier, bool canCrit)` | Heal from a heal-over-time tick. Same math as `Heal`, but `OnHealed` reports it as a tick so combat text can style it differently from direct heals. Returns 0 while `IsDead`: a heal over time that outlives its target never revives it. |
| `bool Revive(int hp)` | Bring a dead unit back with `hp` current HP (clamped to `[1, MaxHP]`). The **only** way HP rises from 0 short of re-seeding the unit via `Initialize`. Fires `VtResourcePool.OnChanged` on the HP pool, then `OnRevived`. Resets the combat timer so the unit comes back out of combat (regen resumes on the next tick). VtAuthority-only. |
| `void ApplyHitFromNet(VtDamageInfo info, bool evaded)` | Raise the hit events for a hit the authority applied: `OnEvaded` when `evaded`, then `OnPostTakeDamage`. Changes nothing; HP arrives through pool replication. Used by replication on clients so hit cues, combat text and interrupts follow the server. Refused on the authority, which raised the events itself. |
| `void ApplyHealFromNet(int amount, bool wasCrit, bool isTick, VtUnitId applier)` | Raise `OnHealed` for a heal the authority applied. Changes nothing. Used by replication on clients; refused on the authority. |
| `void ApplyDeathFromNet(VtUnitId killer)` | Raise `OnDied` and `OnAnyUnitDied` for a death on the authority. Changes nothing; loot, experience and quest credit stay on the authority. Used by replication on clients; refused on the authority. |
| `void ApplyReviveFromNet(int hp)` | Raise `OnRevived` for a revive on the authority. Changes nothing. Used by replication on clients; refused on the authority. |
| `bool SpendResource(VtResourceKind kind, int amount)` | Spend from a specific resource pool. Returns false if the pool doesn't exist or has insufficient current. Runs on the authority and on the owning client, which predicts the cost; the authority's value replicates back. |
| `void RestoreResource(VtResourceKind kind, int amount)` | Restore a specific resource pool. Useful for potions / action-generated rage ticks / etc. VtAuthority-only. HP restores no-op while `IsDead` (a health potion can't be drunk by a corpse); other pools are unaffected by death. |
| `void Tick(float deltaTime)` | Advance the combat timer and the regen scheduler by `deltaTime` seconds. The only time input this component consumes: `Update` forwards `Time.deltaTime` here, and a custom tick driver or dedicated server passes its own step. |
| `VtStatDefinition ResistFor(VtDamageType type)` | Return the `VtStatDefinition` that resists a given `VtDamageType`. Routes through `VtCoreStats.Instance` — returns null when the singleton is missing (damage pipeline treats a null resist stat as zero contribution). |

## VtUnitModifiers

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → Units → VtUnitModifiers**.

Adds up every stat and attribute bonus on a unit. Items, buffs, auras, level growth and innate bonuses each register as a named source; removing a source removes its bonuses, and every change raises `OnModifiersChanged`.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `event Action OnModifiersChanged` | Notification event — fires after any mutation on either channel. Bindings subscribing to it recompute derived values. Safe on both authority and replica sides. Fires exactly once per `Set*/Remove*` call, regardless of which channel was mutated. |
| `void SetSource(string sourceId, VtItemModifier[] modifiers)` | Register or update a secondary-stat source. Passing null or an empty array removes the source. Triggers `OnModifiersChanged`. |
| `void RemoveSource(string sourceId)` | Remove a secondary-stat source by id. No-op if not present. Triggers `OnModifiersChanged` only if a source was actually removed. |
| `bool HasSource(string sourceId)` | True if a secondary-stat source with the given id is currently registered. |
| `float Get(VtStatDefinition stat)` | Total flat bonus for a secondary stat (sum of all flat entries across all secondary sources). Returns 0 if no flat modifiers are present. |
| `float GetPercent(VtStatDefinition stat)` | Total percentage bonus for a secondary stat as a fraction (0.15 = +15%). Returns 0 if none present. |
| `float Apply(VtStatDefinition stat, float baseValue)` | Canonical secondary-stat resolution: `(baseValue + flatSum) * (1 + percentSum)`. |
| `float Apply(VtStatDefinition stat, float baseValue, IReadOnlyList<VtSourceOverride> overrides)` | What `Apply` would return with the sources in `overrides` replaced or removed. Changes nothing and fires nothing. Only direct modifiers are counted: a stat derived from attributes the overridden sources grant is not. |
| `float GetModified(VtStatDefinition stat, float baseValue)` | Additive-only form: `baseValue + flatSum`. Kept for callers that have already factored out percent handling. |
| `float GetMultiplied(VtStatDefinition stat, float baseValue)` | Multiplicative form using only the flat channel: `baseValue * (1 + flatSum)`, for stats that act as a rate multiplier. Prefer `Apply` for new consumers. |
| `void SetAttributeSource(string sourceId, VtAttributeGrant[] grants)` | Register or update a primary-attribute source. Passing null or an empty array removes the source. Triggers `OnModifiersChanged`. |
| `void RemoveAttributeSource(string sourceId)` | Remove a primary-attribute source by id. No-op if not present. Triggers `OnModifiersChanged` only if a source was actually removed. |
| `bool HasAttributeSource(string sourceId)` | True if a primary-attribute source with the given id is currently registered. |
| `float Get(VtAttributeDefinition attribute)` | Total flat point bonus for a primary attribute (e.g. total Strength contributed by baseline + items + buffs). Returns 0 if no grants present. |
| `float GetPercent(VtAttributeDefinition attribute)` | Total percentage bonus for a primary attribute as a fraction (0.10 = +10%). |
| `float Apply(VtAttributeDefinition attribute, float baseValue)` | Canonical primary-attribute resolution: `(baseValue + flatSum) * (1 + percentSum)`. Callers typically use `Mathf.RoundToInt` on the result since primary attributes are int by convention. |

## VtUnitTraits

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → Units → VtUnitTraits**.

Priority-override store for **categorical** traits on a unit — movement type, armor type, attack type, CC flags. Multiple sources (innate / item / buff) can write the same `VtTraitKey` at different priorities; the highest priority wins. The innate default sits at priority 0 so any item or buff that cares will take precedence.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `event Action OnTraitsChanged` | Fires when any trait override changes. Notification event; UI / consumers re-query values on receipt. |
| `void SetTrait<TEnum>(string sourceId, VtTraitKey key, TEnum value, int priority)` | Set an enum-typed trait. Removes any prior entry from the same source for the same key, then appends the new one. |
| `void SetTraitBool(string sourceId, VtTraitKey key, bool value, int priority)` | Set a bool-typed trait (CanAct / CanMove / CanCast). |
| `void SetTraitObject(string sourceId, VtTraitKey key, object value, int priority)` | Set a reference-typed trait (VtProjectileSpec, VtSplashSpec boxed, etc.). |
| `void ClearTrait(string sourceId, VtTraitKey key)` | Remove a single (source, key) override. No-op if missing. |
| `void ClearSource(string sourceId)` | Remove all overrides from a source (e.g. on unequip). Fires event if any were removed. |
| `TEnum GetEnum<TEnum>(VtTraitKey key, TEnum fallback)` | Read an enum-typed trait. Returns `fallback` if no override is set. |
| `bool GetBool(VtTraitKey key, bool defaultValue = true)` | Read a bool-typed trait. Defaults to `defaultValue` (usually `true` for CC flags — no override means "can do it"). |
| `T GetObject<T>(VtTraitKey key)` | Read a reference-typed trait. Returns null if no override is set. |
| `bool HasTrait(VtTraitKey key)` | Low-level: returns whether an override exists for the key. For rare consumers that need to distinguish "no override" from "override with default value". |
| `void ApplyOverrides(string sourceId, VtTraitOverride[] overrides)` | Applies a batch of inspector-authored overrides under a single source id. Used by `VtUnitDefinition.innateTraits` and `VtBuffDefinition.traitOverrides`. |

## VtUnitBuffs

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → Units → VtUnitBuffs**. Adds [VtUnitModifiers](#vtunitmodifiers) automatically.

The buffs and debuffs active on a unit: apply and remove them, ask what is active and for how long, and listen for changes. While a buff is active its stat modifiers, attribute grants and trait overrides apply to the unit, and its tick effects run.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtBuffScheduler Scheduler { get; }` | The buff scheduler behind this component, for advanced use. The members on this component cover normal use. |
| `IReadOnlyList<VtBuffScheduler.Instance> ActiveBuffs { get; }` | The active buff instances, for UI. Do not modify the list. |
| `event Action<VtBuffScheduler.Instance> OnBuffAdded` | Raised when a new buff instance starts on this unit. |
| `event Action<VtBuffScheduler.Instance> OnBuffRemoved` | Raised when a buff instance ends: it expired, was removed or was dispelled. |
| `event Action<VtBuffScheduler.Instance> OnBuffRefreshed` | Raised when re-applying a buff resets or extends an existing instance instead of adding a new one. |
| `VtBuffScheduler.Instance ApplyBuff(VtBuffDefinition def, float duration, VtUnitId applier, bool fromAura = false)` | Apply a buff to this unit for `duration` seconds and return the instance, or null if it was refused. A crowd-control buff whose `VtBuffDefinition.ccCategory` is in the unit's `VtUnitDefinition.ccImmunities` is refused and shows Immune combat text; buffs with no crowd-control category always apply. `fromAura` marks the buff as coming from an aura so UI shows it as lasting; leave it false for a normal apply. |
| `int RemoveBuff(VtBuffDefinition def, bool all = true)` | Remove buff instances by definition. See `VtBuffScheduler.RemoveBuff`. |
| `VtBuffScheduler.Instance ApplyBuffFromNet(VtBuffDefinition def, float remaining, VtUnitId applier, bool fromAura = false)` | Mirror a buff the authority applied: its modifiers apply here and `OnBuffAdded` fires, but it ticks no effects and never expires on its own. Returns the instance to refresh or remove later. Used by replication on clients; refused on the authority. Pass `fromAura` through from the authority so mirrored aura buffs read the same in the UI on both sides. |
| `void RefreshBuffFromNet(VtBuffScheduler.Instance instance, float remaining)` | Set a mirrored buff's remaining time and raise `OnBuffRefreshed`. Used by replication. |
| `void RemoveBuffFromNet(VtBuffScheduler.Instance instance)` | Remove a mirrored buff and raise `OnBuffRemoved`. Used by replication. |
| `bool HasBuff(VtBuffDefinition def)` | True if at least one instance of the buff is active. |
| `float GetRemainingDuration(VtBuffDefinition def)` | Seconds left on the buff, the longest across its stacked instances, or 0 if it is not active. |
| `void Tick(float deltaTime)` | Advance the buff scheduler by `deltaTime` seconds. |

## VtCombatEngagement

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → Combat → VtCombatEngagement**.

Pure target-engagement mechanics for a unit: hold a target, report in-range state, chase into range via the optional `VtTopDownClickToMove` sibling, and rotate the unit to face the target. Carries no combat logic of its own — damage, cooldowns, and swing-timing live in the ability system (`VtUnitAbilities`).

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Range Padding (`rangePadding`) | `float` | 0.1 | ≥ 0 | Extra padding (world units) added to the range check when deciding whether the target is in range. Prevents micro-jitter at the edge of range where float noise would oscillate between 'in' and 'out'. |
| Repath Interval (`repathInterval`) | `float` | 0.25 | ≥ 0.05 | How often (seconds) ChaseInto re-issues a MoveTo toward a moving target. Only used when a VtTopDownClickToMove sibling is attached. |
| Face Rotation Speed (`faceRotationSpeed`) | `float` | 720 | ≥ 0 | Degrees/sec the unit rotates to face its target when no movement component provides rotation. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `IVtAttackable Target { get; }` | Currently engaged target, or null if idle. |
| `bool HasLiveTarget { get; }` | True if a target is held and it still reports `IVtAttackable.CanBeAttacked` plus a live `IVtAttackable.Transform`. Clears the target lazily if the target has been destroyed. |
| `float DistanceToTargetSqr { get; }` | Planar squared distance to the current target, or +∞ if none. Useful for callers that need the raw distance for sort / priority (consider using `IsInRange` for simple range checks — it is also zero-alloc). |
| `event Action<IVtAttackable> OnTargetChanged` | Fires when `Target` changes (including to null). |
| `void RebindMovement()` | Re-discover the sibling `VtTopDownClickToMove`. Call it after adding a mover to a live unit. |
| `void RebindThreatTable()` | Re-discover the sibling `VtThreatTable` (if any) and refresh the threat-driven retargeting subscription. Idempotent — safe to call any number of times. Called automatically from `Awake`, `OnEnable`, and from `VtThreatTable`'s own `OnEnable` when the table is added after this component already cached its absence. |
| `void SetTarget(IVtAttackable newTarget)` | Set the current target. Pass null to clear. Fires `OnTargetChanged` iff the reference actually changed. |
| `void ClearTarget()` | Clear the current target. Equivalent to `SetTarget(null)`. |
| `bool IsInRange(float range)` | True if the current target is within `range` world units (plus padding) of this unit. False if no target, destroyed target, or out of range. Uses squared distance — zero alloc, zero sqrt. |
| `void ChaseInto(float range)` | Request movement toward the current target until it is within `range`. No-op if there is no target or no movement sibling (AI-driven units manage their own approach). Throttled by `repathInterval` so a moving target does not flood MoveTo calls. |
| `void Tick(float deltaTime)` | Drain the `ChaseInto` repath throttle by `deltaTime` seconds. The only time input this component consumes; `Update` forwards `Time.deltaTime`. |
| `void StopChase()` | Stop any chase this component requested (only meaningful when a `VtTopDownClickToMove` sibling is present). Does not clear the target. |
| `void FaceTarget(float deltaTime)` | Rotate to face the current target by one `deltaTime` step. Uses `VtTopDownClickToMove.RotationSpeed` when the sibling is present, otherwise the `faceRotationSpeed` field. No-op with no target. Pass the same delta the caller was ticked with. |

## VtStatDefinition

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → Units → Stat Definition**.

Designer-authored secondary stat — one ScriptableObject asset per stat (MaxHP.asset, CritChance.asset, ResistFire.asset, …). Carries UI-facing metadata (name + description) and **is itself the runtime identity** — `VtUnitModifiers` keys on the asset reference, not on an enum ordinal.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Id (`id`) | `string` | Empty | Stable string identifier, unique across stats. Saves and network messages refer to stats by it. Lowercase snake_case convention: 'stat.max_hp', 'stat.crit_chance'. Changing it breaks existing saves. |
| Display Name (`displayName`) | `string` | Empty | UI display name. E.g. 'Max HP', 'Critical Hit Chance', 'Fire Resistance'. |
| Description (`description`) | `string` | Empty | Designer / tooltip description. E.g. 'Maximum health. Damage reduces current HP; when HP reaches 0 the unit dies.' |

## VtCoreStats

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → Setup → Core Stats**.

Singleton `ScriptableObject` holding direct references to every `VtStatDefinition` that Vantage's pipeline code hardcodes by id — armor, evade, resistances, crit, lifesteal, and the rest.

### Inspector fields

#### Defense

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Armor (`armor`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `Armor` | Defender's armor rating. Reduces physical damage via the pipeline's armor curve. Pipeline id: stat.armor. |
| Evade Chance (`evadeChance`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `EvadeChance` | Chance to evade an incoming non-tick non-True hit. 0..1 fraction; clamped by VtCombatConstants.MaxEvadeChance. Pipeline id: stat.evade_chance. |
| Resist All (`resistAll`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ResistAll` | Flat resistance that applies to every damage type. Stacks with the per-type resist channel. Pipeline id: stat.resist_all. |
| Resist Physical (`resistPhysical`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ResistPhysical` | Physical-element resistance. Pipeline id: stat.resist_physical. |
| Resist Fire (`resistFire`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ResistFire` | Fire-element resistance. Pipeline id: stat.resist_fire. |
| Resist Cold (`resistCold`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ResistCold` | Cold-element resistance. Pipeline id: stat.resist_cold. |
| Resist Poison (`resistPoison`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ResistPoison` | Poison-element resistance. Pipeline id: stat.resist_poison. |
| Resist Lightning (`resistLightning`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ResistLightning` | Lightning-element resistance. Pipeline id: stat.resist_lightning. |
| Resist Holy (`resistHoly`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ResistHoly` | Holy-element resistance. Often paired oppositionally with Shadow. Pipeline id: stat.resist_holy. |
| Resist Shadow (`resistShadow`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ResistShadow` | Shadow-element resistance. Often paired oppositionally with Holy. Pipeline id: stat.resist_shadow. |
| Resist Arcane (`resistArcane`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ResistArcane` | Arcane-element resistance — mage's raw-magic school. Pipeline id: stat.resist_arcane. |
| Resist Nature (`resistNature`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ResistNature` | Nature-element resistance — druid / shaman school. Pipeline id: stat.resist_nature. |

#### Offense

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Armor Penetration (`armorPenetration`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ArmorPenetration` | Attacker's armor-penetration fraction (0..1). Reduces the defender's effective armor before mitigation. Pipeline id: stat.armor_penetration. |
| Crit Chance (`critChance`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `CritChance` | Chance to land a critical hit on direct damage. 0..1 fraction; clamped by VtCombatConstants.MaxCritChance. Pipeline id: stat.crit_chance. |
| Crit Multiplier (`critMultiplier`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `CritMultiplier` | Additive bonus on top of VtCombatConstants.DefaultCritMultiplier for crit damage scaling. Pipeline id: stat.crit_multiplier. |
| Lifesteal (`lifesteal`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `Lifesteal` | Fraction of applied direct damage healed back to the attacker. 0..1. Pipeline id: stat.lifesteal. |
| Mana Steal (`manaSteal`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ManaSteal` | Fraction of applied direct damage restored to the attacker's MP pool. 0..1. Pipeline id: stat.mana_steal. |
| Damage Bonus (`damageBonus`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `DamageBonus` | Flat + percent scaling applied to rolled basic-attack damage when a basic-attack effect references it. Pipeline id: stat.damage_bonus. |
| Physical Power (`physicalPower`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `PhysicalPower` | Auto-applied to every Melee + Ranged hit (non-Magic, non-True). Pipeline scales the rolled damage by modifiers.Apply(physicalPower, dmg) between crit and element resistance. Drives warrior / hunter / rogue gear scaling. Pipeline id: stat.physical_power. |
| Spell Power (`spellPower`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `SpellPower` | Auto-applied to every Magic-attackType hit (non-True). Same place in the pipeline as physicalPower; drives mage / warlock / cleric gear scaling. Pipeline id: stat.spell_power. |
| Thorns (`thorns`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `Thorns` | Fraction (0..1) of applied damage reflected back at the attacker as Physical/Normal. Filtered by VtCombatConstants.ThornsFilter — default PhysicalOnly. Tick damage does not trigger thorns; reflected hits (source=Reflection) don't chain into another reflection. Pipeline id: stat.thorns. |

#### Timing

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attack Speed (`attackSpeed`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `AttackSpeed` | Multiplier on basic-attack cadence. 0.20 = +20% faster swings. Read by the ability scheduler when an ability has scalesWithAttackSpeed = true. Pipeline id: stat.attack_speed. |
| Attack Range Bonus (`attackRangeBonus`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `AttackRangeBonus` | Flat world-units added to any ability's effective cast range when its scalesWithRangeBonus flag is on. Pipeline id: stat.attack_range_bonus. |
| Cooldown Reduction (`cooldownReduction`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `CooldownReduction` | Cooldown-reduction fraction (0..1). Clamped by VtCombatConstants.MaxCooldownReduction (default 0.80). Applied after attack-speed scaling: a 10s cooldown with 0.5 CDR lands at 5s. Pipeline id: stat.cooldown_reduction. |
| Move Speed (`moveSpeed`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `MoveSpeed` | Locomotion top speed bonus. Read by VtTopDownClickToMove as modifiers.Apply(moveSpeed, VtUnitDefinition.moveSpeed) — flat + percent stack on top of the unit's authored base speed. Pipeline id: stat.move_speed. |

#### World

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vision Radius (`visionRadius`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `VisionRadius` | Sight bonus. Read by VtVisionSource as modifiers.Apply(visionRadius, radius) — flat world units and percent stack on the source's authored radius, for fog of war and network interest. Pipeline id: stat.vision_radius. |
| Gathering Speed (`gatheringSpeed`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `GatheringSpeed` | Extra attack speed on swings against resource nodes, as a fraction added to stat.attack_speed. 0.25 = gather 25% faster. Applies to abilities with scalesWithAttackSpeed, such as the basic attack. Pipeline id: stat.gathering_speed. |

#### Miscellaneous

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Xp Gain Multiplier (`xpGainMultiplier`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `XpGainMultiplier` | Multiplier on XP gained by this unit on mob kills. 0..∞ fraction added to 1. Pipeline id: stat.xp_gain_multiplier. |
| Targeting Priority (`targetingPriority`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `TargetingPriority` | Weighting used by enemy AI target selection. Higher = more attractive to attackers. Pipeline id: stat.targeting_priority. |
| Threat Multiplier (`threatMultiplier`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | `ThreatMultiplier` | Scalar applied to all threat this unit generates (damage / heal / ability). Read by VtThreatAutoSubscriber + VtTauntEffect + VtThreatOnApplyEffect. Default 1.0; tank items / talents grant + flat / + percent on this stat. Pipeline id: stat.threat_multiplier. |

#### Resource Pool Bindings

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Resource Pool Stats (`resourcePoolStats`) | [VtResourcePoolStatBinding](#vtresourcepoolstatbinding)[] | 11 entries | Maps each VtResourceKind to its Max-scaling and Regen-scaling stats. Lets VtResourcePoolConfig infer maxStat / regenStat from the selected kind so consumers don't wire MaxHp.asset on every unit definition. Add a row when introducing a new VtResourceKind. Run Tools → Vantage → Auto-Fill VtCoreStats Pool Bindings to populate. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static VtCoreStats Instance { get; }` | The loaded singleton: the one handed to `OverrideInstance`, else your `Assets/Resources/VtCoreStats.asset`, else the package's. Null only if the shipped asset has been deleted from the package and you have none — which is a configuration error and logs once via the warning below. |
| `VtStatDefinition GetMaxStat(VtResourceKind kind)` | Look up the `VtStatDefinition` that scales pool Max for `kind`. Returns null when no binding exists (caller treats null as "no modifier scaling — use raw baseMax"). Linear scan over a fixed ~12-row array; called per-pool, not per-frame. |
| `VtStatDefinition GetRegenStat(VtResourceKind kind)` | Look up the `VtStatDefinition` that scales pool regen rate for `kind`. Returns null when no binding exists or the kind doesn't passively regen (e.g. Rage / ComboPoints). |
| `static void ResetCache()` | Forgets the cached core stats so the next `Instance` read loads the asset again. Use it after swapping the asset in the editor, or in test teardown after `OverrideInstance`. |
| `static void OverrideInstance(VtCoreStats instance)` | Use `instance` as the core stats, such as a copy a boot scene references. Call it before gameplay starts. Pass null to behave like `ResetCache`. |

## VtAttributeDefinition

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → Units → Attribute Definition**.

Designer-authored primary attribute — one ScriptableObject asset per attribute (Strength.asset, Dexterity.asset, Intelligence.asset, Vitality.asset, Luck.asset, Agility.asset, …). Carries UI-facing metadata (name + description) and **is itself the runtime identity** — `VtUnitModifiers` keys primary-attribute totals on the asset reference. No separate channel / enum / id field is needed.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Id (`id`) | `string` | Empty | Stable string identifier for save files and network payloads. Empty = the asset name. |
| Display Name (`displayName`) | `string` | Empty | UI display name. E.g. 'Strength', 'Intelligence', 'Luck'. |
| Description (`description`) | `string` | Empty | Tooltip / codex description shown on the character sheet or allocation UI. E.g. 'Physical power. Each point grants +1 melee damage and +2 max HP.' |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `string SaveId { get; }` | Id for save files and commands: `id`, or the asset name when empty. |

## VtAttributeFormula

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → Units → Attribute Formula**.

Designer-tunable mapping from primary attributes (authored as `VtAttributeDefinition` assets) to any derived `StatType`. Fully data-driven — each entry is one (source attribute → target stat) row with a per-point coefficient. Add, remove, or reassign rows in the inspector without touching code.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mappings (`mappings`) | [VtAttributeFormula.Mapping](#vtattributeformulamapping)[] | Empty | All attribute→stat contribution rules. One attribute can appear in many rows (multi-effect), and one target stat can appear in many rows (multi-source). |

## VtAttributeDerivedStatsBinding

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → Units → VtAttributeDerivedStatsBinding**. Adds [VtUnitModifiers](#vtunitmodifiers), [VtUnit](#vtunit) automatically.

Optional binding that reads primary-attribute totals from `VtUnitModifiers`' primary channel and projects them into secondary stats (MaxHP, DamageBonus, CritChance, …) under modifier-source id `"attr"`. This is the seam where the two channels meet: sources from the primary side, targets on the secondary side, one-way flow.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Formula (`formula`) | [VtAttributeFormula](#vtattributeformula) | None | Designer formula — rows of (source attribute → target stat, per-point) tuples. Leave null / empty to disable all derived-stat projection. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `void Refresh()` | Re-seed the attribute baseline from the current definition and recompute the derived stats. Call it after swapping the `VtAttributeFormula` or changing the unit's definition at runtime. |

## VtBuffDefinition

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → Units → Buff Definition**.

Designer-authored description of a single buff / debuff. Referenced from code (`VtUnitBuffs.ApplyBuff`) or from scriptable asset chains (perks, equipped items with "on-hit apply X"). Fully data-driven — creating a new buff is an inspector action, no C#.

### Inspector fields

#### Identity

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Id (`id`) | `string` | Empty |  | Machine id used for stack resolution. Two assets with the same id are treated as the same buff. |
| Display Name (`displayName`) | `string` | Empty |  | UI display name. |
| Description (`description`) | `string` | Empty |  | Tooltip / codex description. |
| Icon (`icon`) | `Sprite` | None |  | Icon for buff bar / tooltip. |
| Icon Id (`iconId`) | `string` | Empty |  | An icon from the Vantage icon set by name, such as shield or flame, drawn when Icon is empty, so a buff has art on the buff bar before its own sprite exists. |
| Harmful (`harmful`) | `bool` | Off |  | A debuff: it works against the unit that carries it, such as a burn or a slow. Buff bars and unit frames mark it and its tooltip names it a debuff. |

#### Effects

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Modifiers (`modifiers`) | [VtItemModifier](#vtitemmodifier)[] | Empty |  | Secondary-stat modifications applied while the buff is active (HPRegen, CritChance, Armor, ResistFire, ...). |
| Attribute Grants (`attributeGrants`) | [VtAttributeGrant](#vtattributegrant)[] | Empty |  | Primary-attribute grants applied while the buff is active (+5 STR, +10% INT, ...). |
| Trait Overrides (`traitOverrides`) | [VtTraitOverride](#vttraitoverride)[] | Empty |  | Categorical overrides (movement type, armor type, CC flags, ...). Priority is set per-entry; typical buff priority is 200. |
| Tick Effect (`tickEffect`) | [VtTickEffect](#vttickeffect) | — |  | Optional periodic effect — DoT / HoT. Leave amountPerTick = 0 to disable. |

#### Presentation

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Applied Cue (`appliedCue`) | [VtPresentationCue](presentation.md#vtpresentationcue) | — |  | Animator trigger, sound and effect played on the target when the buff is applied. |
| Removed Cue (`removedCue`) | [VtPresentationCue](presentation.md#vtpresentationcue) | — |  | Played when the buff expires or is removed. |
| Loop Vfx Prefab (`loopVfxPrefab`) | `GameObject` | None |  | Effect prefab kept on the target for as long as the buff lasts. Optional. |

#### Duration

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default Duration (`defaultDuration`) | `float` | 5 | ≥ 0 | Seconds the buff lasts if ApplyBuff is called with duration <= 0. |
| Max Duration (`maxDuration`) | `float` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Only used for StackAddDuration policy — the cap on combined duration. 0 = no cap. |
| Stacking Policy (`stackingPolicy`) | [VtStackingPolicy](#vtstackingpolicy) | `Refresh` |  | How re-application behaves when an instance already exists. |

#### Crowd Control

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cc Category (`ccCategory`) | [VtCcCategory](#vtcccategory) | `None` |  | Categorical CC label. Routes the apply attempt through VtUnit.IsImmuneTo(VtCcCategory) — if the target is immune, the buff is silently rejected (and an Immune combat-text event fires for visible feedback). Pure stat / damage buffs use None and skip the gate entirely. |

## VtUnitTagDefinition

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → Units → Unit Tag Definition**.

Designer-authored categorical label for a unit — e.g. `Undead.asset`, `Beast.asset`, `Humanoid.asset`, `Construct.asset`, `Demon.asset`. Attach to a `VtUnitDefinition`.tags array to declare what a unit *is*; consumers (quest objectives, vs-type items, bestiary UI, targeting filters) query via `VtUnit.HasTag(tag)`.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Id (`id`) | `string` | Empty | Stable string identifier for DB / network payloads. Convention: 'tag.undead', 'tag.beast'. |
| Display Name (`displayName`) | `string` | Empty | UI display name. E.g. 'Undead', 'Beast', 'Humanoid'. |
| Description (`description`) | `string` | Empty | Lore / tooltip description. E.g. 'Reanimated corpses. Vulnerable to Holy damage, immune to Fear.' |

## VtDefinitionCatalog

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → Setup → Definition Catalog**.

Turns the string ids that travel in save files and network messages back into definition assets. Create one with **Create → Vantage → Setup → Definition Catalog**, drag your definitions in, and save it as `Assets/Resources/VtDefinitionCatalog.asset` so `Instance` finds it. Both sides of a network connection need the same catalog.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Abilities (`abilities`) | [VtAbilityDefinition](abilities.md#vtabilitydefinition)[] | Empty | Every ability a client may ask the server to cast. |
| Buffs (`buffs`) | [VtBuffDefinition](#vtbuffdefinition)[] | Empty | Buffs saved or replicated by id. |
| Items (`items`) | [VtItemDefinition](items.md#vtitemdefinition)[] | Empty | Items saved or replicated by id. |
| Units (`units`) | [VtUnitDefinition](#vtunitdefinition)[] | Empty | Unit definitions saved or replicated by id. |
| Quests (`quests`) | [VtQuestDefinition](quests.md#vtquestdefinition)[] | Empty | Quests saved or replicated by id. |
| Currencies (`currencies`) | [VtCurrencyDefinition](currency.md#vtcurrencydefinition)[] | Empty | Currencies saved or replicated by id. |
| Recipes (`recipes`) | [VtRecipeDefinition](crafting.md#vtrecipedefinition)[] | Empty | Recipes saved or replicated by id. |
| Crafting Skills (`craftingSkills`) | [VtCraftingSkillDefinition](crafting.md#vtcraftingskilldefinition)[] | Empty | Crafting skills saved or replicated by id. |
| Buildables (`buildables`) | [VtBuildableDefinition](building.md#vtbuildabledefinition)[] | Empty | Buildables, so saved buildings can be spawned again from their prefab. |
| Talents (`talents`) | [VtTalentDefinition](progression.md#vttalentdefinition)[] | Empty | Talents saved or replicated by id. |
| Attributes (`attributes`) | [VtAttributeDefinition](#vtattributedefinition)[] | Empty | Attributes saved or replicated by id (the asset name when the id is empty). |
| Unlocks (`unlocks`) | [VtUnlockDefinition](unlocks.md#vtunlockdefinition)[] | Empty | Unlocks saved or replicated by id. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static VtDefinitionCatalog Instance { get; }` | The catalog at `Resources/VtDefinitionCatalog`, or null with one warning when there is none. |
| `static void OverrideInstance(VtDefinitionCatalog catalog)` | Use `catalog` as the instance, such as one a boot scene references. Null restores the Resources lookup. |
| `void Rebuild()` | Rebuild the lookups after changing the arrays at runtime. |
| `bool TryGetAbility(string id, out VtAbilityDefinition definition)` | Find an ability by id. |
| `bool TryGetBuff(string id, out VtBuffDefinition definition)` | Find a buff by id. |
| `bool TryGetItem(string id, out VtItemDefinition definition)` | Find an item by id. |
| `bool TryGetUnit(string id, out VtUnitDefinition definition)` | Find a unit definition by id. |
| `bool TryGetQuest(string id, out VtQuestDefinition definition)` | Find a quest by id. |
| `bool TryGetCurrency(string id, out VtCurrencyDefinition definition)` | Find a currency by id. |
| `bool TryGetRecipe(string id, out VtRecipeDefinition definition)` | Find a recipe by id. |
| `bool TryGetCraftingSkill(string id, out VtCraftingSkillDefinition definition)` | Find a crafting skill by id. |
| `bool TryGetBuildable(string id, out VtBuildableDefinition definition)` | Find a buildable by id. |
| `bool TryGetTalent(string id, out VtTalentDefinition definition)` | Find a talent by id. |
| `bool TryGetAttribute(string id, out VtAttributeDefinition definition)` | Find an attribute by id. |
| `bool TryGetUnlock(string id, out VtUnlockDefinition definition)` | Find an unlock by id. |
| `void BuildableCategories(List<VtBuildableCategoryDefinition> results)` | Fill `results` with every category the catalog's buildables use, lowest `Sort Weight` first, then by name. Buildables without a category are not represented; list them with `BuildablesInCategory` and a null category. |
| `void BuildablesInCategory(VtBuildableCategoryDefinition category, List<VtBuildableDefinition> results)` | Fill `results` with the catalog's buildables in `category`, lowest `Sort Weight` first, then in catalog order. A null category lists the buildables that have none. |
| `void RecipeCategories(List<VtRecipeCategoryDefinition> results)` | Fill `results` with every category the catalog's recipes use, lowest `Sort Weight` first, then by name. |
| `void RecipesInCategory(VtRecipeCategoryDefinition category, List<VtRecipeDefinition> results)` | Fill `results` with the catalog's recipes in `category`, lowest `Sort Weight` first, then in catalog order. A null category lists the recipes that have none. |

## VtResourcePoolConfig

Serializable struct.

Inspector-authored configuration for one `VtResourcePool` on a unit. A `VtUnitDefinition` carries an array of these; at spawn, `VtUnitStats` instantiates a live `VtResourcePool` for each entry using these values as seeds.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kind (`kind`) | [VtResourceKind](#vtresourcekind) | `HP` |  | Kind of resource (HP / MP / Stamina / Rage / ...). |
| Base Max (`baseMax`) | `int` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Base max value before modifiers. The live Max resolves as VtUnitModifiers.Apply(maxStat, baseMax). |
| Starting Current (`startingCurrent`) | `int` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Starting current value. Usually equal to baseMax; set lower for units that start wounded. |
| Regen Mode (`regenMode`) | [VtRegenMode](#vtregenmode) | `None` |  | How and when this pool regenerates. |
| Base Regen Per Second (`baseRegenPerSecond`) | `float` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Starting regen-rate baseline (per second) before modifiers. Final rate = this + VtUnitModifiers.Get(regenStat). |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtStatDefinition maxStat` | Optional per-pool override for the Max-scaling stat. Leave null and the kind→stat binding on VtCoreStats supplies the right asset (HP → MaxHp, etc.). Hidden by default — set programmatically only when one specific unit needs a custom max-scaling stat (e.g. a boss whose MaxHp scales off a tagged stat). |
| `VtStatDefinition regenStat` | Optional per-pool override for the Regen-scaling stat. Leave null and the kind→stat binding on VtCoreStats supplies the right asset. Hidden by default; see maxStat for the override use case. |

## VtItemModifier

Serializable struct.

A single stat modification that an item / buff / perk / innate provides to a unit. Summed into `VtUnitModifiers`'s two channels (flat and percent) per `VtStatDefinition` reference, then applied by consumers as `(base + flatSum) * (1 + percentSum)`.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stat (`stat`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | None | Which stat this entry modifies. Pick from the dropdown of every VtStatDefinition asset in the project (core + consumer-authored). |
| Value (`value`) | `float` | 0 | If isPercentage is false, added flat. If true, treated as a fraction (0.10 = +10%). |
| Is Percentage (`isPercentage`) | `bool` | Off | Flat (false) → added to base. Percentage (true) → multiplied against (base + flatSum). |

## VtAttributeGrant

Serializable struct.

One contribution to a unit's primary-attribute total, flat or percent. Unit definitions use it for the starting attributes, items for "+5 Strength" bonuses, and buffs for temporary grants.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attribute (`attribute`) | [VtAttributeDefinition](#vtattributedefinition) | None | Which primary attribute this grant contributes to. Pick from the dropdown of every VtAttributeDefinition asset in the project. |
| Value (`value`) | `float` | 0 | If isPercentage is false, added flat. If true, a fraction of the resolved total (0.10 = +10%). |
| Is Percentage (`isPercentage`) | `bool` | Off | Flat (false) — adds to the attribute's point total. Percentage (true) — scales the resolved total by (1 + sum of percent grants). |

## VtAttributeGrowth

Serializable struct.

Per-level growth rate for a single primary attribute — "+2 Strength per level", "+1.5 Intelligence per level". Authored on `VtUnitDefinition`. `VtAttributeDerivedStatsBinding` reads this on enable and on every level-up, projecting `(level - 1) * perLevel` into the primary-attribute channel under source id `"attr_growth"`.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attribute (`attribute`) | [VtAttributeDefinition](#vtattributedefinition) | None | Which primary attribute grows each level. Drag in an VtAttributeDefinition asset. |
| Per Level (`perLevel`) | `float` | 0 | Attribute points gained per level above 1. Typical ranges - primary attribute 2.0-3.0, secondary 1.0-1.5. Zero disables growth for this attribute without removing the row. |

## VtTraitOverride

Serializable struct.

One categorical trait override — declared on a buff / item / innate so that the `VtUnitTraits` aggregator can pick the highest-priority non-null value for each `VtTraitKey`.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Key (`key`) | [VtTraitKey](#vttraitkey) | `VtMovementType` | Which trait this entry sets. |
| Priority (`priority`) | `int` | 0 | Priority — highest wins if multiple sources write the same key. Innate defaults = 0, equipped items ≈ 100, buffs ≈ 200. |
| Movement Value (`movementValue`) | [VtMovementType](#vtmovementtype) | `Walk` | For VtMovementType trait. |
| Armor Value (`armorValue`) | [VtArmorType](#vtarmortype) | `Unarmored` | For VtArmorType trait. |
| Attack Value (`attackValue`) | [VtAttackType](#vtattacktype) | `Normal` | For VtAttackType trait. |
| Damage Value (`damageValue`) | [VtDamageType](#vtdamagetype) | `Physical` | For VtDamageType trait (e.g. convert-to-fire buff). |
| Bool Value (`boolValue`) | `bool` | Off | For CanAct / CanMove / CanCast bool traits. |

## VtTickEffect

Serializable struct.

Describes a periodic "tick" that runs while a buff is active — damage-over-time (poison, bleed, burn) or heal-over-time (regeneration aura). `VtUnitBuffs` schedules the tick and routes the resulting damage through the normal `VtUnitStats.TakeDamage` pipeline so resistances / armor / hooks all apply naturally.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Amount Per Tick (`amountPerTick`) | `float` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Damage (or heal if isHeal=true) applied per tick. 0 = disabled. |
| Interval (`interval`) | `float` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Seconds between ticks. 0 = disabled. |
| Damage Type (`damageType`) | [VtDamageType](#vtdamagetype) | `Physical` |  | Element routed through the target's resistance channel. Use True to bypass mitigation. |
| Attack Type (`attackType`) | [VtAttackType](#vtattacktype) | `Normal` |  | Matrix axis for the tick. Default-flat matrix → no impact unless your game extends VtAttackType + populates matrix cells. |
| Channel (`channel`) | [VtDamageChannel](#vtdamagechannel) | `Melee` |  | Class channel for the tick — Magic for spell-class DoTs/HoTs (default), Melee/Ranged for weapon-class bleeds. Drives power-stat scaling. |
| Is Heal (`isHeal`) | `bool` | Off |  | When true, ticks call Heal instead of TakeDamage. VtDamageType is still used to tag the heal source for any 'increased fire healing' edge cases. |
| Can Crit (`canCrit`) | `bool` | Off |  | If true, each tick rolls crit from the applier's stat.crit_chance and amplifies by stat.crit_multiplier (+ VtCombatConstants.DefaultCritMultiplier). Applies to both DoT ticks (damage) and HoT ticks (heal). Off by default — only buffs whose author explicitly wants per-tick crit variance turn it on. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `bool IsActive { get; }` | Whether this tick effect is effectively enabled. |

## VtSplashSpec

Serializable struct.

Declarative specification of a splash / AoE effect. Lives on weapons (`ItemDefinition.splash`), innate attacks (`VtUnitDefinition.splash`), and projectiles (`VtProjectileSpec.splash`). A `radius` of 0 means "no splash (single-target)".

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Radius (`radius`) | `float` | 0 | ≥ 0 | World-space radius around the impact point. 0 = single-target. |
| Falloff (`falloff`) | `AnimationCurve` | None |  | Damage-multiplier curve. x axis [0,1] = normalized distance from impact, y axis [0,1] = fraction of primary damage delivered. Default curve = 1→0 linear. |
| Friendly Fire (`friendlyFire`) | `bool` | Off |  | If false, units sharing the attacker's VtFaction are skipped. |
| Target Mask (`targetMask`) | `LayerMask` | Nothing |  | Which physics layers to scan for targets. Set to the unit collider layers. |
| Cone Angle (`coneAngle`) | `float` | 0 | 0 to 360 | Full cone angle in degrees. 360 (default) = full circle (bomb / fireball). < 360 = cone in front of attacker (cleave / whirlwind). Candidates whose angle from attacker.forward exceeds coneAngle/2 are skipped. Ignored when the attacker is null (environmental splash — always full circle). |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `bool IsActive { get; }` | True if this spec represents an active splash effect. |
| `float EffectiveConeAngle { get; }` | The cone angle in effect: 0 (unset) and 360 both mean a full circle; any value in between is a cleave cone in front of the attacker. |

## VtProjectileSpec

Serializable struct.

Declarative config for a ranged attack's visible projectile. Lives on innate unit attacks (`VtUnitDefinition.projectile`) and can be overridden per-weapon by items via `VtTraitKey.ProjectileKind`.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefab (`prefab`) | `GameObject` | None |  | Visual prefab spawned at the attacker's muzzle. Must carry a projectile-driver component. Leave null for instant-hit / hitscan attacks. |
| Speed (`speed`) | `float` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Travel speed in world units / second. Final speed = this + VtUnitModifiers.Get(ProjectileSpeed stat). |
| Arc Height (`arcHeight`) | `float` | 0 | ≥ 0 | Parabolic arc peak height in world units. 0 = straight line (arrow / bullet). >0 = ballistic arc (catapult / lobbed spell). Peak occurs at the midpoint of the travel path. |
| Homing (`homing`) | `bool` | Off |  | If true, the projectile tracks the target each frame — adjusts direction to follow moving targets (homing missile, guided arrow). If false, it flies straight toward the target's position at launch (arrow, bullet) — target can dodge by moving. Arcing + homing combo is supported but looks physically odd; prefer one or the other per projectile. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `bool IsActive { get; }` | True if this spec describes a travelling projectile (prefab assigned). |

## VtDamageInfo

Class.

The per-hit damage payload carried through the damage pipeline. A **class**, not a struct — so mutation hooks (`VtUnitStats.OnPreTakeDamage`, `VtUnitStats.OnPreDealDamage`) can convert element, accumulate absorb, or cancel the hit entirely.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `float rawAmount` | Damage amount *after* crit multiplication, *before* mitigation. Mutated in place by the pipeline (resistance, matrix, armor, absorb) and finally rounded to an int for HP subtraction. |
| `VtDamageType type` | Element of the attack. Routes through the corresponding `ResistX` stat. `VtDamageType.True` bypasses all mitigation. |
| `VtAttackType attackType` | Matrix axis. Keyed with the defender's `VtArmorType` into the `VtDamageMatrix` for a multiplier. Default is `VtAttackType.Normal`; consumers extend the enum + populate matrix cells for unit-counter mechanics. Pure RTS-flavor; default flat matrix means this field is a tag with no damage-math impact. |
| `VtDamageChannel channel` | RPG class channel — Melee, Ranged, or Magic. Hardwired axis that drives power scaling in the pipeline (Magic → spellPower; Melee / Ranged → physicalPower), gear restrictions, animation hooks, and procs that key off "what kind of attack was this." Independent of `attackType`: a poisoned dagger is `channel = Melee, attackType = Normal`; a fireball is `channel = Magic, attackType = Normal`. |
| `VtDamageSource source` | How this damage was delivered (melee / ranged / ability / DoT / ...). Used by procs and conditional modifiers. |
| `VtAbilityDefinition ability` | Ability that produced this damage, when one did. Presenters play its impact cue on the target. |
| `VtUnitId attacker` | Id of the attacking unit, or `VtUnitId.None` for environmental. Resolved via `VtUnitRegistry.Resolve` when a live reference is needed. |
| `Vector3 hitPoint` | World-space impact point (for VFX / floating-number anchor). |
| `float absorbed` | Damage pre-consumed by absorb / shield subscribers to `VtUnitStats.OnPreTakeDamage`. The pipeline subtracts this before rounding. |
| `bool wasCrit` | True if the attacker's crit roll succeeded. Set by the attacker side before calling `VtUnitStats.TakeDamage`. |
| `bool ignoreArmor` | If true, the armor-reduction step is skipped. Useful for piercing mechanics that bypass the `Armor` stat but still respect resistance. |
| `bool isTickDamage` | Flag set by tick effects (DoT/HoT). The pipeline skips the evade roll for tick damage — DoTs always land once they're applied. |
| `bool tickCanCrit` | If true, a tick-damage hit is still eligible for the crit roll. Set by `VtBuffScheduler` from `VtTickEffect.canCrit` when the buff's tick author opted in. Has no effect on non-tick damage, which always rolls crit. |
| `bool cancelled` | A pre-hook may set this to `true` to drop the hit entirely (block / immunity / phase-out). The pipeline fires `VtUnitStats.OnPostTakeDamage` for accounting and returns 0. |
| `int appliedDamage` | Final integer damage applied to HP after the pipeline completes. Set by `VtUnitStats.TakeDamage` just before firing `VtUnitStats.OnPostTakeDamage` so UI / log subscribers can read it. |

## VtUnitId

Serializable struct.

Stable identity for a `VtUnit` that is safe to store in cross-system data (`VtDamageInfo.attacker`, event args, log entries). The underlying value has no semantic meaning other than "unique per live unit in this process".

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `bool IsValid { get; }` | True for any id other than `None`. |
| `static readonly VtUnitId None` | "No unit": the attacker of environmental damage, or an unknown source. |
| `readonly int Value` | Raw integer id. Do not derive meaning from its magnitude. |

## VtUnitRegistry

Static class.

Resolves `VtUnitId` values to live `VtUnit` instances. Units register when they are enabled or seeded and unregister when disabled or destroyed; entries whose unit was destroyed without either callback are dropped the next time the registry is read, so `All` never yields a dead unit.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static int Count { get; }` | Number of live units. |
| `static IEnumerable<VtUnit> All { get; }` | Every live unit. Destroyed units are skipped and pruned. |
| `static VtUnitId Register(VtUnit unit)` | Allocate a fresh id for `unit`. |
| `static void Unregister(VtUnitId id)` | Remove the mapping for `id`. No-op when unknown. |
| `static VtUnit Resolve(VtUnitId id)` | The live unit for `id`, or null when unknown or destroyed. Callers must null-check: a stale id from a delayed callback is expected. |
| `static void Prune()` | Drop entries whose unit has been destroyed. |

## VtFactionRules

Static class.

The one rule the package uses to decide whether two factions fight: different factions are hostile unless either side is `VtFaction.Neutral`. Neutral units (resource nodes, vendors, critters) never attack and are never attacked on sight; the player must target them deliberately, which `CanAttackOnCommand` decides.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static bool AreHostile(VtFaction a, VtFaction b)` | True when units of faction `a` and `b` attack each other on sight. |
| `static bool CanAttackOnCommand(VtFaction attacker, VtUnit target)` | True when a unit of faction `attacker` may attack `target` on a deliberate command such as a right-click or an attack order: the factions are hostile, or a component on the target implements `IVtCommandAttackable` and accepts the attacker. Resource nodes accept every attacker until they are depleted. |

## IVtAttackable

Interface. Implemented by [VtUnit](#vtunit).

Marker contract: anything the player / AI can target for damage. Implemented by `VtUnit` (players, enemies, NPCs) and by non-unit damageables (destructible buildings, training dummies, props). Interaction systems work against this interface rather than concrete unit classes.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `Transform Transform { get; }` | World-space transform used for positioning / distance checks. |
| `bool CanBeAttacked { get; }` | False to refuse attacks (already dead, phase-invulnerable, owned by same team, etc.). |
| `int TakeDamage(int damage)` | Apply flat damage. Returns the amount actually dealt (for hit feedback / XP). |

## IVtCommandAttackable

Interface. Implemented by [VtResourceNode](resource-nodes.md#vtresourcenode).

A component on a unit that lets players attack the unit on purpose although its faction is not hostile to them. Resource nodes implement it so a right-click or an attack order chops a Neutral tree; implement it on props, doors or practice targets that should take deliberate attacks. It changes nothing about attacks on sight: idle units and AI still fight only hostile factions, see `VtFactionRules.CanAttackOnCommand`.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `bool CanBeAttackedOnCommand(VtFaction attacker)` | True when a unit of faction `attacker` may attack this unit on a deliberate command. |

## VtResourcePoolStatBinding

Serializable struct.

Maps a `VtResourceKind` to the `VtStatDefinition` assets that scale its pool's `Max` and `Regen` values. Authored on `VtCoreStats` as the canonical kind→stat lookup so consumers don't have to wire `VtResourcePoolConfig.maxStat` / `VtResourcePoolConfig.regenStat` on every `VtUnitDefinition` — selecting `kind = HP` already implies "use MaxHp / HpRegen."

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kind (`kind`) | [VtResourceKind](#vtresourcekind) | `HP` | Resource kind this row applies to (HP / MP / Stamina / ...). |
| Max Stat (`maxStat`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | None | VtStatDefinition asset that scales the pool's max value (e.g. MaxHp.asset). Leave empty if this kind has no max-scaling stat. |
| Regen Stat (`regenStat`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | None | VtStatDefinition asset that scales the pool's regen rate (e.g. HpRegen.asset). Leave empty if this kind doesn't passively regen (Rage, ComboPoints, etc.). |

## VtAttributeFormula.Mapping

Serializable struct.

One contribution row — a single attribute's per-point effect on a single derived stat.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source Attribute (`sourceAttribute`) | [VtAttributeDefinition](#vtattributedefinition) | None | Source primary attribute. Drag in an VtAttributeDefinition asset (Strength / Dexterity / Intelligence / ...). |
| Target Stat (`targetStat`) | [VtStatDefinition](#vtstatdefinition) | None | Derived stat this row contributes to (drag in a VtStatDefinition asset: MaxHp.asset, DamageBonus.asset, CritChance.asset, ...). |
| Per Point (`perPoint`) | `float` | 0 | Per-point contribution. Example: 10 means each source-attribute point grants 10 of the target stat. |
| Is Percentage (`isPercentage`) | `bool` | Off | If false, contribution is flat (adds to target). If true, contribution is a percentage fraction (0.01 = +1%). |

## Enums

### VtFaction

Team or allegiance of a `VtUnit`. Units of different factions fight each other unless either is Neutral; AI targeting, splash damage and projectiles all respect it.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Neutral` | Unaffiliated or ambient — not targeted, not hostile. |
| `Player` | The local player and their summons / pets. |
| `Enemy` | Scripted hostile units (waves, bosses). |
| `Wildlife` | Passive NPCs (deer, rabbits) — flee when attacked, don't aggro. |

### VtCcCategory

Categorical label for crowd-control buffs. Authored on `VtBuffDefinition.ccCategory`; read by the apply-time immunity gate (`VtUnit.IsImmuneTo`) and by per-game UX systems (CC bar, breaking-CC procs, diminishing returns).

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `None` | Not crowd control. Pure stat / damage buffs use this. |
| `Stun` | Cannot act (no movement, no cast, no attack). Bash / Hammer of Justice. |
| `Root` | Cannot move; can still attack and cast. Frost Trap / Entangling Roots. |
| `Silence` | Cannot cast spells / abilities; can move and auto-attack. Counterspell. |
| `Disarm` | Cannot use weapon / auto-attack; can still cast spells. Disarm shout. |
| `Fear` | Forced random / fleeing movement, no player input. Howl of Terror. |
| `Charm` | Faction temporarily flipped — unit fights on the caster's side. Mind Control. |
| `Sleep` | Cannot act until damage breaks the effect. Sleep / Hibernate. |
| `Polymorph` | Visual transform + cannot act / cast (often heals while polymorphed). Polymorph. |
| `Slow` | Movement speed reduced. Slow / Frostbolt's debuff. NOT a hard CC. |
| `Knockback` | Forced horizontal displacement. Shockwave / Death Grip-source. |
| `Knockup` | Forced vertical displacement (lifted off ground). Knockup. |
| `Taunt` | Forced target swap on AI controllers. Taunt / Mocking Blow. |

### VtDamageType

The *element* of an attack — routed through the corresponding `resistX` stat on `VtCoreStats` in `VtUnitStats.TakeDamage`.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Physical` | Weapons, claws and falling rocks. Reduced by armor; resisted by stat.resist_physical. |
| `Fire` | Fire and burning. Resisted by stat.resist_fire. |
| `Cold` | Frost and ice. Resisted by stat.resist_cold. |
| `Poison` | Poison and venom, often dealt over time. Resisted by stat.resist_poison. |
| `True` | Bypasses all mitigation (resistance, armor, matrix). Use sparingly. |
| `Lightning` | Electricity / chain-lightning / EMP-flavor. Resisted by stat.resist_lightning. |
| `Holy` | Paladin / priest school. Strong vs undead in many genres. Resisted by stat.resist_holy. |
| `Shadow` | Warlock / necromancer school — corruption, agony, void. Resisted by stat.resist_shadow. Often paired oppositionally with Holy. |
| `Arcane` | Mage's "raw magic" school — distinct from elemental. Magic missile, polymorph. Resisted by stat.resist_arcane. Conventionally hardest to resist. |
| `Nature` | Druid / shaman school — earth, plant, weather, wildlife. Resisted by stat.resist_nature. |

### VtAttackType

The *matrix / unit-counter axis* of a hit — paired with the defender's `VtArmorType` in `VtDamageMatrix` to produce a multiplier. Pure RTS-flavor mechanic; default matrix is flat (every cell 1.0) for MMO/ARPG scope.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Normal` | Default attack type. The matrix lookup against any armor type returns 1.0 (no multiplier) when the matrix is flat. Use as the catch-all when your game doesn't care about unit-counter mechanics. |

### VtDamageChannel

The *class / source channel* of a hit — i.e. how it was delivered from the character-fantasy point of view. Hardwired and stable: the pipeline, gear procs, tooltips, and animation systems all key off these three values.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Melee` | Touch-range weapon strikes — swords, daggers, fists, staves, hammers. |
| `Ranged` | Projectile / thrown weapons — bows, guns, throwing knives, javelins. |
| `Magic` | Casted spells — bolts, novas, missiles, channels, curses. |

### VtArmorType

The *defender-side* armor classification — paired with the attacker's `VtAttackType` in the `VtDamageMatrix` for a multiplier. Default matrix is flat (MMO scope), so these values mainly serve as categorical tags (gear tiers, loot filters, encounter design) that content systems can read without the matrix affecting damage math.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Unarmored` | No armor — naked, cloth-less. Mage robe / clothwearer default. |
| `Light` | Leather, padded — light caster / rogue armor. |
| `Medium` | Chainmail, scale — mid-tier hunter / shaman armor. |
| `Heavy` | Plate — warrior / paladin armor. |

### VtResourceKind

The kind of a resource pool on a unit, such as health, mana, stamina or rage. A unit definition lists the pools it has; read one with `VtUnitStats.GetPool`.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `HP` | Health. The unit dies when it reaches 0. |
| `MP` | Mana, spent by spells. |
| `Stamina` | Stamina, spent by physical actions such as sprinting or dodging. |
| `Rage` | Rage, built by dealing and taking damage rather than regenerating. |
| `Focus` | Focus, a small fast-refilling pool for ranged or precise actions. |
| `Energy` | Energy, a fixed-size pool that refills quickly. |
| `ComboPoints` | Combo points, built by some abilities and spent by finishers. |
| `Charges` | Charges, discrete uses that refill one at a time. |
| `Hunger` | Food pool: decreases over time, damages HP when empty. |
| `Thirst` | Water pool: decreases over time, damages HP when empty. |
| `Shield` | Secondary HP layer — sci-fi / mage-barrier style. Regenerates out of combat (per the configured `VtRegenMode`); takes damage before HP only when consumer code wires that interception (typically via an `VtUnitStats.OnPreTakeDamage` hook). Pair with `stat.max_shield` / `stat.shield_regen`. |

### VtTraitKey

Keys used by `VtUnitTraits` to identify which categorical trait a `VtTraitOverride` is setting. Each key corresponds to a specific value type that consumers expect back when reading; mismatching types is a programmer error.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtMovementType` | How the unit moves; the value is a `global::VtMovementType`. |
| `VtArmorType` | The unit's armor type; the value is a `global::VtArmorType`. |
| `VtAttackType` | The unit's attack type; the value is a `global::VtAttackType`. |
| `VtDamageType` | The element of the unit's attacks, for "your attacks deal Fire" buffs; the value is a `global::VtDamageType`. |
| `ProjectileKind` | The projectile the unit's basic attack fires; the value is a `VtProjectileSpec`. |
| `Splash` | Splash damage on the unit's attacks; the value is a `VtSplashSpec`. |
| `CanAct` | Can the unit take ANY action (attack, cast, move)? Stun = false. |
| `CanMove` | Can the unit move? Root = false (but can still attack/cast). |
| `CanCast` | Can the unit cast spells / abilities? Silence = false. |

### VtStackingPolicy

How a new application of a buff interacts with an existing instance of the *same* `VtBuffDefinition`. Resolved inside `VtUnitBuffs.ApplyBuff`.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Unique` | If already present, do nothing. The existing buff keeps its remaining duration. |
| `Refresh` | If already present, reset the duration to the new value but don't add a second instance. Most common policy for re-applied DoTs. |
| `StackIndependent` | Always add another independent instance. Each instance ticks and expires separately. Used when a DoT from two different attackers should stack. |
| `StackAddDuration` | If already present, add the new duration to the remaining duration (capped by the buff's `maxDuration` if set). Classic RPG "stack duration" rule. |

### VtRegenMode

Describes *how* a `VtResourcePool` refills over time. Picked per-pool per-unit in the `VtResourcePoolConfig` so e.g. HP trickles passively, Rage generates on attack, and Stamina refills only when out of combat.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `None` | No automatic regen. Only external calls (potions, abilities) restore it. |
| `Passive` | Always regenerates at the `regenStat` rate (per second). |
| `CombatOnly` | Regenerates only while the unit is in combat — used for resources like Rage / Energy that build up *while* fighting. |
| `OutOfCombatOnly` | Regenerates only while the unit is OUT of combat — classic resting-heals rule for Stamina / HP in many RPGs. |
| `OnActionGenerated` | Does not passively tick — instead is *generated* by specific actions (landing an attack, dodging, spending another resource). Callers push into it via `VtResourcePool.Restore` at the action site. |

### VtMovementType

Categorical movement capability — resolved via `VtUnitTraits` under `VtTraitKey.VtMovementType`. A binding component (e.g. `MovementTypeBinding`) reads the current value and configures the pathfinder accordingly (flyers ignore cliffs, swimmers navigate water, etc.).

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Walk` | Moves on the ground and is blocked by cliffs and obstacles. |
| `Fly` | Flies over terrain and obstacles. |
| `Swim` | Moves through water. |
| `Hover` | Floats just above the ground, over water and low obstacles. |

### VtDamageSource

Classifies *how* a piece of damage was delivered: a melee or ranged attack, an ability, damage over time, reflection or the environment. Carried on every `VtDamageInfo` so procs, conditional bonuses and UI can tell hits apart.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `None` | Unknown / unset. Treat as generic damage. |
| `MeleeAttack` | Basic melee attack from a weapon or unarmed. |
| `RangedAttack` | Basic ranged attack (bow, thrown weapon). |
| `Ability` | Active spell / skill / ability damage (usually consumes MP or a charge). |
| `DoT` | Periodic damage tick from a `VtBuffDefinition.tickEffect`. |
| `Reflection` | Damage reflected back at the attacker (thorns, retaliation, reactive spells). |
| `Environmental` | World damage — lava, spikes, fall damage, starvation. |
| `Splash` | A secondary hit from an AoE / splash resolution. |
